system:
You merge the reading-pass results for the divisions of one work into one cast. You get, for each division, its characters and locations (id, name, aliases, note, and for characters a possible same_person_as link) and the titles of the sections each one appears in.

Return:
1. characters: one entry per individual across the whole work. Merge division entries that are the same individual, even when the divisions used different ids or names. Entries that name each other (one's same_person_as points at the other, or one's aliases include the other's name) are candidates to be one individual: merge them when the notes and the story support it, and otherwise keep them apart and say why in the note. Keep entries apart when they are different individuals who share a name; never join entries on a shared name alone. The note is one line saying who this is and how to tell them apart. `members` lists every merged division entry as "division:id".
2. locations: the same, for places. Two places are one entry only when they are the same place, not when one is inside the other.

Every division entry must appear in exactly one merged entry's members. Use short, stable snake_case ids.

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective of 221B Baker Street, narrated through Watson's eyes; present throughout the cases in these divisions and the one who solves each.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion, a doctor; first-person voice throughout these divisions.

characters.name: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein
characters.note: Hereditary King of Bohemia who visits Baker Street disguised as Count Von Kramm to recover his photograph with Irene Adler; distinct from the Bohemian royal figures of other stories.

characters.name: Irene Adler
characters.note: Former opera contralto and adventuress of Briony Lodge who marries Godfrey Norton and flees to the Continent.

characters.name: Godfrey Norton
characters.note: Barrister of the Inner Temple who visits Irene Adler and becomes her husband; not to be confused with other Norton-named figures.

characters.name: John
characters.note: Irene Adler's coachman sent to watch Holmes; distinct from the cabman and stable-boy John of the Man With the Twisted Lip.

characters.name: Mrs. Turner
characters.note: Landlady at Baker Street; distinct from Mrs. Hudson, the landlady of other stories.

characters.name: Mary Jane
characters.note: Watson's careless servant mentioned in passing by Holmes's deductions; distinct from the other Mary characters.

characters.name: the elderly woman
characters.note: Elderly servant at Briony Lodge who tells Holmes the lady has left for the Continent.

characters.name: the loungers
characters.note: Group of confederates staging the street quarrel and false fire alarm on Holmes's orders.

characters.name: the slim youth in an ulster
characters.note: Unidentified youth who greets Holmes by name in the street at the end of the Bohemia story.

characters.name: Jabez Wilson
characters.note: Stout, red-haired pawnbroker of Saxe-Coburg Square who brings the Red-Headed League case.

characters.name: Vincent Spaulding
characters.note: Clean-shaven assistant of Wilson who is really John Clay's accomplice in disguise; distinct from the criminal leader Clay.

characters.name: Duncan Ross
characters.note: Small red-headed man running the League office at Pope's Court under a false identity, allied with Clay.

characters.name: John Clay
characters.note: Royal-blooded young thief and forger who tunnelled from the pawnshop cellar to the bank; arrested in the vault.

characters.name: Archie
characters.note: Red-haired accomplice of John Clay who escapes down the hole.

characters.name: Peter Jones
characters.note: Official police agent from Scotland Yard who hunts with Holmes in the Red-Headed League case.

characters.name: Mr. Merryweather
characters.note: Solemn chairman of the bank directors of the City and Suburban Bank branch, and a whist player.

characters.name: Miss Mary Sutherland
characters.note: Typewriting young woman whose missing fiancé Hosmer Angel is her stepfather in disguise; distinct from the Mary of other stories, and the Miss Sutherland mentioned in Red-Headed League only in passing.

characters.name: Ezekiah Hopkins
characters.note: Deceased American millionaire who founded the Red-Headed League; referred to only.

characters.name: Mr. James Windibank
characters.note: Mary Sutherland's stepfather who secretly disguised himself as her fiancé Hosmer Angel to prevent the marriage; Hosmer Angel is not a real person in the story.

characters.name: Mrs. Sutherland
characters.note: Widow who remarried Windibank and was in on the deception; not on stage.

characters.name: Mr. Hardy
characters.note: Former foreman of Mary's late father's business; mentioned only.

characters.name: Mrs. Watson
characters.note: Watson's wife, appearing only at the opening of The Man With the Twisted Lip and in the Boscombe breakfast scene.

characters.name: Lestrade
characters.note: Ferret-like Scotland Yard detective; appears in the Boscombe and Noble Bachelor cases.

characters.name: Alice Turner
characters.note: Daughter of John Turner who hires Holmes in the Boscombe Valley case; distinct from Alice the maid of the Noble Bachelor case.

characters.name: James McCarthy
characters.note: Son of Charles McCarthy, accused of killing his father in the Boscombe Valley case.

characters.name: Charles McCarthy
characters.note: Former convict driver, tenant of Hatherley Farm, and murder victim by the pool.

characters.name: John Turner
characters.note: Wealthy landowner of the Hall and the actual killer in the Boscombe Valley case.

characters.name: William Crowder
characters.note: Game-keeper employed by Turner who witnessed McCarthy walking alone.

characters.name: Patience Moran
characters.note: Fourteen-year-old daughter of the lodge-keeper who saw the McCarthys quarrelling.

characters.name: Dr. Willows
characters.note: Physician attending John Turner.

characters.name: John Cobb
characters.note: Groom and servant of McCarthy; mentioned only.

characters.name: Moran, the lodge-keeper
characters.note: Lodge-keeper of the Boscombe Valley estate, father of Patience Moran.

characters.name: the barmaid
characters.note: Bristol barmaid whom James secretly married; mentioned only.

characters.name: John Openshaw
characters.note: Young client, nephew of Colonel Elias Openshaw, found drowned near Waterloo Bridge; not to be confused with his uncle.

characters.name: Colonel Elias Openshaw
characters.note: Uncle of John Openshaw, former Confederate colonel who dies in a garden pool after the K.K.K. warning; not to be confused with John.

characters.name: Joseph Openshaw
characters.note: Brother of Colonel Elias and father of John; dies falling into a chalk-pit.

characters.name: Major Prendergast
characters.note: Army officer who referred Openshaw to Holmes; mentioned only.

characters.name: Mr. Fordham
characters.note: Horsham lawyer who witnessed the colonel's will; mentioned only.

characters.name: Major Freebody
characters.note: Commander of a fort on Portsdown Hill; mentioned only.

characters.name: Captain James Calhoun
characters.note: Master of the barque Lone Star and leader of the K.K.K. gang; never on stage.

characters.name: Police-Constable Cook
characters.note: H Division constable who heard the cry near Waterloo Bridge; mentioned only.

characters.name: Hudson
characters.note: Name in the colonel's 1869 diary page; mentioned only.

characters.name: McCauley
characters.note: Name in the 1869 diary page; mentioned only.

characters.name: Paramore
characters.note: Name in the 1869 diary page; mentioned only.

characters.name: John Swain
characters.note: Name in the 1869 diary page; mentioned only.

characters.name: Mary
characters.note: Household servant at Horsham; mentioned only.

characters.name: Isa Whitney
characters.note: Brother of Elias Whitney and opium addict found in an opium den; husband of Kate Whitney.

characters.name: Kate Whitney
characters.note: Wife of Isa Whitney who comes to Watson's house asking for help.

characters.name: Malay attendant
characters.note: Attendant at the opium den who offers Watson a pipe.

characters.name: Lascar manager
characters.note: Keeper of the opium den in Upper Swandam Lane.

characters.name: Dane assistant
characters.note: Assistant at the opium den; mentioned only.

characters.name: Neville St. Clair
aliases: the beggar with the twisted lip
characters.note: Respectable Lee gentleman who disguised himself as the beggar Hugh Boone; Hugh Boone is the same person and is merged here.
